promptAsSent:
Use the image_gen tool to generate exactly one image, then stop. Do not write files, run commands or edit anything.

Attached reference images, in order:
Image 1: Geometry/layout authority: every block's size, position, outline and lens
Image 2: Material/style only; not layout

Asset: a sheet of four separate top-down tactical-game sprites: the ceiling light fixtures of an abandoned Domain-era megastructure plant in a spacefaring civilization, seen from directly below the ceiling looking up is NOT wanted: they are drawn as seen from directly above (orthographic, 90 degrees, no perspective), as a top-down battle map shows a ceiling lamp, for the Starsector Marines battle map. One block-out frame is one map cell, about one soldier wide; the fixtures are small inside it.
Geometry: reference 1 is the layout authority. Reskin each grey block-out in place: keep every fixture exactly inside its block, at its size, position and outline; do not move, enlarge, merge or add pieces. The lighter grey area in each block is the lens: keep the lens exactly where and as large as it is drawn. Transparent space stays fully transparent.
State: every fixture is UNLIT and long dead: its lens is dark, dusty, faintly tinted glass (warm grey for the two white ceiling lamps, dark oxblood red for the two emergency lamps), no glow, no light, no bloom.
Style: match reference 2 (the same plant's works-hall kit) for material: crisp painterly-pixel game sprite, gunmetal and blue-gray industrial steel, dark seams, small bolts, worn ochre trim, adult military sci-fi, heavy and utilitarian; detail that still reads when shrunk to 128 px a cell. Not cartoon, no thick outlines.
View: strictly top-down. Soft upper-left object-local light.
Background: true transparent background with clean alpha; no ceiling, floor, base tile, shadow slab, border, labels or text.

Subjects, left to right:
1. ceiling-strip: an industrial caged strip lamp: a long steel housing with mounting brackets at each end, a long diffuser lens behind a welded wire guard cage.
2. ceiling-highbay: a round high-bay lamp: a heavy round steel reflector rim around a round domed lens, a spoked wire guard across it.
3. emergency-strip: a short emergency strip lamp: a compact armoured housing with end brackets around a narrow red lens.
4. emergency-beacon: an emergency beacon: a small caged dome lamp with a red lens on a square bolted mounting plate.
